metadata.synopsis: The SJC sustained Psiaki’s complaint and held that the CPC Session erred by ordaining and installing officers elected at a February 5, 2023 congregational meeting where the congregation’s bylaw excluded communing members under 18 from voting. Reading BCO 6-4, 25-1, and 25-7 together, the SJC ruled that all communing members are entitled to vote and that local bylaws cannot impose an age restriction; the “good and regular standing” language addresses censure, not age. The decision did not annul the completed ordination/installation, but required future elections and installations to comply with the Constitution.

1. Did the Session of Covenant Presbyterian Church err in its understanding and application of BCO 57-2 in denying the request of Dr. and Mrs. Frank Chin to examine their young children for admission to the sealing ordinances?

BCO 57-2 does not require a Session to examine every young person put forward by parents for admission to the sealing ordinances. We affirm that the Presbytery and the CPC Session correctly understood and applied BCO 57-2.

BCO 57-2 leaves the determination of “the time when young persons come to understand the Gospel" to the “prudence of the Session." This section does not impose upon a Session a mandate to examine every young person brought before it.

It is our judgment that the CPC Session acted within its constitutional discretion in concluding that “the time" had not yet come for examination of Dr. and Mrs. Chin's children. BCO 57-2 places the emphasis where it belongs—upon the “prudence of the Session"
We cannot agree with the majority's Opinion finding that Covenant Presbytery (CP) did not err in its understanding and application of BCO 57-2.

metadata.synopsis: The Chins complained to the SJC after Covenant Presbytery denied their complaint against Covenant Presbyterian Church Session's refusal to examine their young children for admission to the Lord's Supper. The SJC did not sustain the complaint. Its adopted reasoning held that BCO 57-2 leaves the time for examining young persons to the Session's prudence and imposes no mandate to examine every child put forward; if the Session decides the time has come, careful examination is required. The dissent read BCO 57-1 as requiring examination of covenant children seeking admission.
